review.why: Explains about seventy mental models and cognitive biases with a marketing application for each, from anchoring and social proof to pricing psychology.
review.summary: Groups models into thinking tools, buyer psychology, persuasion, pricing psychology, design and delivery, and growth. Each entry has a short definition and a concrete application. A quick reference table maps common problems (low conversion, price objections, churn) to the models that fit, and five questions steer the choice.
strengths: Every model has a concrete marketing application
Repeatedly reminds the user to apply tactics only when genuine
cautions: Some popular figures (loss aversion twice as strong, seven touchpoints) are heuristics, not firm findings
A few tactics, such as decoys and door-in-the-face, can mislead if used carelessly
No sources or tests are cited
